statement: In a pond, 80% of the fish are carp. Some of the carp are taken out, and no other fish are added or removed. Now 50% of the fish in the pond are carp. What percentage of the carp were taken out?

choices.misconception: I subtracted 50 from 80, treating the drop in percentage points as the share of carp removed.
I thought the carp went from 80 to 50 out of the same 100 fish, so 30 of the 80 carp were removed.
I found that 40 fish are left out of the original 100 and gave that instead.
I found that 60 fish were removed and gave that as a percentage of all the fish, not of the carp.

hints: Which fish do not change in number?
Imagine 100 fish at the start. The other fish are not touched, so their number stays the same, but they become a larger share of the pond. Use them to find the new total.
There are 20 other fish. After the removal they make up 50% of the pond, so the pond holds 40 fish.

solutions.reliable: Start with 100 fish: 80 carp and 20 others. The 20 others stay, and afterwards they make up 50% of the pond, so the pond now holds 40 fish, of which 20 are carp. So 80 - 20 = 60 carp were taken out, which is 60/80 = 75% of the carp. The transferable idea: when percentages change, anchor on the quantity that does not change.

whyOnTest: Percentage-change questions test anchoring on the part that stays fixed, because the total itself changes.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
